svg.aria-label: Three panels. Panel a shows six broad overlapping bell-shaped tuning curves across a stimulus direction axis; a dashed line marks the true stimulus at 150 degrees, green bars give the six evoked firing rates as a population activity profile, and an annotation notes that 100 such neurons read out over 250 milliseconds give an estimate about nineteen times sharper than the width of any one tuning curve. Panel b shows a step stimulus above two responses: a slowly adapting response that peaks and then settles to a sustained plateau, and a rapidly adapting response that fires only at the onset and the offset of the step. Panel c plots firing rate against stimulus intensity over ten decades, comparing a logarithmic code that assigns ten hertz to every decade with a linear code that leaves nine of the ten decades below ten hertz.

g.text: Transduction and coding: three facts that recur in every modality
Broad tuning curves, sharp population estimate
Adaptation is a high-pass filter: dynamic range
bought by discarding the absolute level.
A linear code leaves 9 of 10 decades below 10 Hz.
